It is 50% more volatile/sensitive than the market index

explanation.text: The Logic: Source p.148 defines beta as the sensitivity of a stock or portfolio return to the market index. A beta greater than one means the stock is more volatile than the benchmark, so beta = 1.5 implies the stock is roughly 50% more sensitive/volatile than the market index. The Trap: A lower-volatility stock would have beta less than 1; beta = 1.5 does not mean zero or no market risk. Note: Beta measures sensitivity to the market, not total risk.
